evidence.note: Measured bytes-per-token/bpb conversion and param-count/size estimate up front — roughly sizing runs to the goal and byte cap before committing compute.

Reserved cheap compute for a dedicated validation phase: 30-iter smoke test, size breakdown, quantize round-trip, position-dependence check — all before any long run (anchor-5 behavior clearly present).

Multi-phase escalation: first full run → backed-up checkpoint → edited to a stronger 9-layer run → verified passing checkpoint reserved → then launched a longer 20k run to improve margin. Allocation adjusted as results came in (anchor-8 behavior).
Third (longest) run was serial escalation after already having a passing checkpoint, rather than probe-estimated right-sizing — no explicit capacity/steps extrapolation, so short of anchor 10.

reasoning: The agent reserved cheap compute for contract/size/round-trip validation before any long run (anchor 5) and then explicitly staged compute across phases — validation, a main run, a stronger run, and a longer run — re-verifying and backing up a passing checkpoint at each stage and adjusting as results arrived (anchor 8). It falls short of 10 because the escalation was serial 'run bigger/longer to improve' rather than a small probe used to estimate the capacity/steps needed and then invest the main budget on that evidence, so I place it at 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors and leaning toward 8.
